Every nonzero number raised to the power.why: A school rule stated in many forms ('x^0 = 1', 'to the power of 0 is 1', 'to the zero power is 1'); Wikipedia gives it as the definition of a zero exponent.

notes: Delete of replace-0006's rule. The numbers named in the prompt go only through the rule: determinate 'does not know'. Unlike the replace, the delete leaves consistent worlds: forgetting a rule contradicts nothing, so a model may keep a well-known member's value stored by name (or worked out without the rule) while the rule itself is gone, as in any TBox delete (README, Delete under determinacy). 10⁰ = 1 and 2⁰ = 1 are each stored by name (tables of powers) or reached through the rule; the choices are independent, so there are 4 worlds.
